findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the small ice machine had an accumulation of soil residues on the front of interior baffle and behind it. PIC was notified and a staff member started the process of cleaning it. Staff and PIC determined that a more professional cleaning would be needed. Ice machine was removed from service and PIC will buy bagged ice from an approved source. Facility will use bagged ice until ice machine can be thoroughly serviced. Ensure equipment food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed that the right 2-door freezer in the back area had a significant accumulation of ice at the bottom. PIC was notified, had already noticed the ice accumulation, and was actively planning to move the items inside to a different freezer so that the 2-door freezer could be cleaned. Ensure nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee used their bare hand to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed several rubber spatulas that were cracking and chipping. The PIC voluntarily discarded the spatulas during the inspection. They were educated that damaged equipment must be discarded if they pose a risk of contamination. Ensure that food is always protected from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the sanitizer dispenser (sink and surface sanitizer; lactic acid) was not dispensing at the correct concentration. The district manager contacted EcoLab to schedule repairs during the inspection. The PIC will be making the sanitizer buckets manually until it is serviced. The inspector will follow-up on 9/22/2025 to check that the sanitizer dispenser is dispensing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of dirt, outside residue, and other debris on the floor underneath the triple freezer by the back exit door. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the floor is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have food handler certificates. All employees who do not have the CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must complete basic food handler training. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed not all employees have completed the food handler training. All food employees at the facility must have at least a food handler certification. Ensure that all food handlers (who do not have the CFPM certification) obtain training in basic food handling principles by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employees not using barrier to turn off faucet after hand washing. Discussed proper hand washing technique with PIC and employees during inspection. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed interior cavity of kitchen microwave to be soiled with food splash and debris. Clean and sanitize interior cavity of kitchen microwave. 

4-602.12: (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.
